description:
FOUND s490 (Fable) at the s473t6b review, by the batch's one companion `--all --quick --jobs 2` on the final tree (log ~/pcl-agent-scratch/s490/review/t6b-companion.log).

Since #1850 (s473t6b: the harness's TAP is on disk row by row) a file the runner KILLS at its timeout keeps every row that ran.  For a file that HANGS at a fixed point that figure is deterministic and the snapshot comparison is as good as before: op/gv.t read TIMEOUT 90/95 and uni/gv.t TIMEOUT 75/84 in the parallel pass AND the #366 serial re-run (both spliced, cause #1850).  For a file that is merely SLOWER than its allowance the figure is HOW FAR IT GOT, which is a function of the box's load:

  uni/variables.t   C_ok 1300 in all three measurements; C_notok 18760 (parallel, --jobs 2), 25743 (the overnight member-0 run), 29351 (serial re-run, recorded in the snapshot)

so the SNAPSHOT block will report it THREE-WAY on every run from now on, and s488a's whole point (#1834) was that this block is QUIET unless something moved.  Before #1850 the same file flapped less only because most of its rows died in the buffer.

FIX SHAPE (pick by measurement, not here): (a) a TIMEOUT-status snapshot row compares STATUS + C_ok only when the file is registered as RATE-LIMITED (a column or a marker in baselines/perl-suite-timeouts.tsv, which already owns per-file allowances), printing the notok figure without judging it; or (b) give the file the allowance it needs (it is 66,880 perl rows; measure how long PCL takes alone -- if it is minutes, (a)).  MEASURE FIRST: list every TIMEOUT row in baselines/perl-suite-run.tsv and classify hang-at-a-fixed-row (stable; two runs agree) vs rate-limited (unstable) -- today that is 3 files, and only uni/variables.t is of the second kind.

Runner-only (tools/run-perl-suite.pl + its tools/t guard); no product change.  Related: #1850, #1834/#1835 (s488a), #366 (the serial re-run), #1651 (the gv.t hang).
subject: Companion SNAPSHOT: a RATE-LIMITED TIMEOUT file's C_notok is load-dependent now that every row reaches disk (#1850) -- uni/variables.t reads 18760 / 25743 / 29351 failing rows in three runs at a stable C_ok 1300, so the block s488a made quiet will flag it THREE-WAY on every run
